content.comment_body: I am trying to set up a solution that identifies when the Ethernet connection between [product_name] modules is lost. Once the communication drops, I want to trigger a flag to indicate the issue. If anyone has sample code or suggestions, I’d appreciate your help. Thank you in advance.

In my projects, I monitor the network using a life signal. Additionally, I employ a network input configured as a diagnostic bit, which uses the Ethernet link error type. See the attached file for reference.

Thanks for your help. I have reviewed your example, which sends a pulse over the network and checks if the receiving logic detects it. However, using a diagnostic network input seems simpler. I have tried the diagnostic type approach previously, but it didn’t work for me. I’ll give it another attempt.
The diagnostic bit won’t identify every type of network error. That’s why I use it as an additional measure. The most reliable method remains life signal monitoring.
Alright, I understand now. Thank you again for the clarification.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing methods to detect and indicate lost Ethernet connectivity between [product_name] modules. Two main strategies are mentioned: using diagnostic network input for link errors and a more reliable approach using life signal monitoring. There is some uncertainty about the effectiveness of the diagnostic function, highlighting possible limitations of built-in features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a simple and effective way to detect and signal Ethernet connection loss between [product_name] units, preferring solutions that use built-in diagnostics or straightforward logic.
